title: <svg> nodes drop their own box paint (background, padding, radius, border, ring, shadow) and the glyph is scaled to the border box
evidence: paint-mobile-cards: three quick-action icons 'h-12 w-12 rounded-full bg-indigo-100 p-3' (one with ring-2, one with border-2 + shadow-md) render as bare 48px glyphs with no circle or tile, and the icon is drawn at 48px instead of the 24px content box. paint-effects: 'filter: drop-shadow' on the star SVG is lost too.
rootCause: ui.html walk() → svgNode(el, box) never calls boxVisual() and serializes the clone at the border-box size. Padding and border are ignored, and code.js createNode() returns the bare createNodeFromSvg frame.
verifierNotes:
I confirmed the gap in the code and by re-running the harness.

Code:
- In ui.html, walk() handles SVG with `case 'SVG': return leaf(svgNode(el, box))`. This returns before boxVisual() is ever called, so the element's background, border, radius, box-shadow/ring and filter are never collected.
- svgNode() serializes the clone with width/height set to the border box (`clone.setAttribute('width', box.w)`). It strips class/style, and SHAPE_PROPS contains only fill/stroke properties, so padding and border never reach the output. Chrome draws an outer <svg>'s viewBox into its CONTENT box, so with padding the glyph comes out too big.
- In code.js, shapeNode() has an SVG branch that only names and resizes the node. It never calls applyBox, so even fills placed on an SVG tree node would be ignored.
- Nothing in ui.html parses filter drop-shadow(). boxVisual only takes blur() from filter, so the drop-shadow claim is also real.

Harness (paint-mobile-cards, diff 4.07%):
- dev/out/paint-mobile-cards.json has three SVG nodes, each {w:48,h:48} with no fills/effects, viewBox 0 0 24 24, width=48 height=48.
- orig.png shows a 48px indigo circle, an emerald circle with a ring, and an amber rounded tile with a border and shadow, each with a roughly 24px glyph.
- render.png shows bare glyphs drawn at 48px with no circles or tiles.
- This is not a renderer artifact: the tree itself carries no paint, so real Figma would show the same thing.

Impact: Tailwind output like `<svg class="h-10 w-10 rounded-full bg-x-100 p-2">` is less common than wrapping the icon in a div, but it does occur, and when it does the result is clearly broken (lost badge, glyph at double size). Medium severity is right.

The proposed fix is mostly right, with four gaps:
1. When there is padding but no paint, there is no need for a wrapper. Just place the bare SVG at the content box.
2. drop-shadow needs separate placement. CSS filters the whole rendered element. With no background the shadow takes the glyph's shape, so the effect belongs on the SVG node (a Figma frame without fills casts its shadow from its children). That needs a code.js change, because the SVG branch of shapeNode ignores effects.
3. The wrapper should keep the svg's opacity/absolute (`common`) and its name. Since the SVG elements stay leaves of the same border-box size, the parent's Auto Layout detection is unchanged.
4. The default `svg:not(:root){overflow:hidden}` UA rule makes visual.clip true. That is fine on the wrapper, which then clips to its radii.

Unverified side observation, not part of this finding: svgNode copies computed colors verbatim. Under Tailwind v4 the JSON shows stroke="oklch(0.511 0.262 276.966)". The headless renderer (Chrome) draws that correctly, but Figma's createNodeFromSvg may not parse oklch(), which could turn Tailwind v4 icons black or invisible in real Figma. A cheap safeguard is to send fill/stroke/stop-color through parseColor() and write them back as rgb()/hex. This needs checking in real Figma.

title: Box styles on a <svg> element (background, padding, border-radius, border, shadow/ring) are dropped, and the icon is drawn over the padding
evidence: media-tw-icons: `<svg class="h-12 w-12 rounded-lg bg-indigo-600 p-3 text-white">` (the Tailwind UI feature-icon pattern) comes out as a white icon on white, so it is invisible. The emerald icon loses its bg-emerald-100 circle and ring-4. The amber one loses its border-2, background and shadow-md. In all three the glyph is drawn 48px wide instead of 24px (content box). Compare orig.png and render.png around y=100-160.
rootCause: ui.html walk(): `case 'SVG': return leaf(svgNode(el, box))` never calls boxVisual(). svgNode sets width/height to the border-box size, so the viewBox is mapped onto border+padding instead of the content box.
verifierNotes:
I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs media-tw-icons` (diffPct 24.99, 0 mockErrors) and looked at the crops of orig.png and render.png at y≈60-220.

- **Indigo icon:** the original shows a 48px indigo rounded square with a white glyph. The render shows nothing, because the white glyph sits on a white page.
- **Emerald icon:** the light-emerald circle and its ring are missing. The lock glyph is drawn about 48px tall instead of about 28px.

In the JSON, each of the three icons is a bare node `{type:'SVG', w:48, h:48}`. Its serialized `<svg>` has `viewBox="0 0 24 24"` and `stroke="rgb(255,255,255)"`, and carries no background, radius, border or effects.

The cause is in `walk()` in ui.html. `case 'SVG': return leaf(svgNode(el, box))` returns before `boxVisual()` runs. `svgNode()` only copies SHAPE_PROPS (fill/stroke/…) and then removes class and style from the clone. It sets the clone's width/height to the border-box, so the viewBox is stretched over padding+border. On the code.js side, `shapeNode()` for an SVG only resizes and never calls `applyBox()`. The gap is real, comes from the plugin, and is not a renderer artifact.

Problems with the proposed fix:
1. `edges(cs)` does not exist in ui.html, so padding and border have to be computed inline.
2. Chrome's UA stylesheet gives every non-root `<svg>` `overflow:hidden`. That makes `visual.clip` true for every inline SVG. So the trigger must be `visual.has || padding/border > 0` and must not involve clip. Otherwise every icon on every page gets an extra wrapper frame, which is a regression in layer count and naming.
3. `common` (absolute, opacity) must go on the wrapper, not on the inner SVG. Otherwise the absolute flag and opacity get applied twice.
4. When there is no viewBox, `svgNode`'s fallback (`w0 = width attr || box.w`) must use the content box.

Severity: when the pattern appears, the result is very visible (an invisible icon). But most AI- and Tailwind-generated markup puts the bg and padding on a wrapping `<div>`, not on the `<svg>` itself, so this is medium rather than high.

Separate observation, not verified: the computed colors baked into the SVG are Tailwind v4 `oklch(...)` strings. The harness renders those in Chrome, which understands them. Figma's `createNodeFromSvg` parser may not accept oklch(). If so, it would fail or draw black there, and the harness would not catch it. Converting colors to rgb() inside `svgNode` (e.g. via `parseColor`) is worth checking separately.

title: SVG paint attributes are written as oklch()/oklab()/color() strings (Tailwind v4 currentColor), which Figma's SVG importer likely cannot parse
evidence: paint-mobile-cards JSON: svg nodes carry stroke="oklch(0.511 0.262 276.966)", and the same happens for every Tailwind v4 text-* color on currentColor icons. Not yet confirmed in Figma; the harness renders through Chrome, which understands oklch, so the problem is invisible here. Figma's createNodeFromSvg is not known to support CSS Color 4 functions, so icons may import black or unpainted.
rootCause: ui.html svgNode(): `val = scs.getPropertyValue(p)` is copied verbatim into fill/stroke/stop-color attributes. Only url() references and px units are rewritten.
verifierNotes:
I checked this in the code and it holds up. In ui.html, svgNode() loops over SHAPE_PROPS/STOP_PROPS and copies scs.getPropertyValue(p) straight into the cloned SVG's attributes. The only rewrites are url(#id) and dropping the px unit. Chrome keeps CSS Color 4 syntax in computed fill and stroke values. Tailwind v4 colors are oklch(), and its /opacity modifiers turn into oklab() or color(srgb ...) through color-mix. So SVG strings like stroke="oklch(0.511 0.262 276.966)" end up in the tree. The existing outputs confirm it: dev/out/paint-mobile-cards.json, paint-effects.json, layout-zorder-transforms.json, layout-grid-stacking.json and gen-tw-controls.json all contain oklch() in SVG paint attributes.

code.js passes n.svg unchanged to figma.createNodeFromSvg. dev/mock-figma.js only checks that the string starts with <svg, and the renderer is Chrome, which reads oklch fine. That is why the harness can't show the problem (diffPct looks clean). I didn't run the case in real Figma. But Figma's SVG importer is a separate parser that handles hex, rgb()/rgba() and named colors, and nothing indicates it supports CSS Color 4. Under SVG rules an unparseable paint is invalid. That means fill goes back to black and stroke goes back to none. Lucide and Heroicons icons are stroke-based and colored with currentColor plus Tailwind text-* classes, so they would likely show up invisible or black. That pattern is on almost every v0/shadcn/Claude-generated Tailwind v4 page, so high severity is justified. Evidence level: the code path is confirmed and the oklch strings are in the JSON. What Figma does with them is very likely, but I didn't check it in Figma.

The proposed fix is right in direction, but has three problems:
(a) The loop sets attributes in SHAPE_PROPS order: fill, fill-opacity, …, stroke, stroke-width, stroke-opacity. If you multiply alpha into fill-opacity while handling fill, the later fill-opacity pass overwrites it with the computed value. Paint and opacity have to be handled together.
(b) parseColor() returns null both for 'transparent' and for strings it can't parse. Mapping null to 'none' could break unusual values such as context-stroke.
(c) The last part, about colors kept in a 'style' attribute, does nothing. svgNode already calls d.removeAttribute('style') and d.removeAttribute('class') on every element.

Regressions: hex plus opacity is the same color for anything inside sRGB. Out-of-gamut oklch gets clamped by the canvas path that parseColor already uses for the rest of the plugin, so behavior stays consistent. The Chrome-based harness renderer will look the same. No Figma API change is needed. code.js stays as it is.

title: SVG paints are baked as oklch()/color() strings, which Figma's SVG importer cannot parse (affects every Tailwind v4 icon)
evidence: In dev/out/media-tw-icons.json the SVG nodes carry fill="oklch(0.596 0.145 163.22)" and fill="oklch(0.551 0.027 264.36)" on the root and children. Tailwind v4 (the CDN the plugin injects) defines its whole palette in oklch, so every currentColor icon (text-gray-500, text-emerald-600 ...) ends up like this. The harness re-renders SVG in Chrome, which understands oklch, so the diff hides the bug. Figma's SVG parser only takes hex/rgb/named colors, so these icons import black or unfilled.
rootCause: ui.html svgNode(): copies scs.getPropertyValue(p) verbatim for fill/stroke/stop-color. getComputedStyle keeps the authored color space (oklch, lab, color(display-p3 ...)) and does not normalize to rgb.
verifierNotes:
I checked this myself and the gap is real. ui.html svgNode() (lines 939-969) loops over SHAPE_PROPS/STOP_PROPS (line 163) and calls d.setAttribute(p, scs.getPropertyValue(p)). The only changes it makes are rewriting url() and stripping px. Colors are never normalized. The current dev/out/media-tw-icons.json has SVG strings such as `<svg ... fill="oklch(0.596 0.145 163.225)" ...>`, with 8 oklch occurrences. oklch also shows up in SVG payloads for tailwind-snippet, paint-mobile-cards, paint-effects, gen-tw-controls, layout-grid-stacking and layout-zorder-transforms. The plugin injects Tailwind v4 (TAILWIND_CDN = @tailwindcss/browser@4, line 1140), whose palette is defined in oklch. Opacity modifiers like text-gray-500/50 resolve through color-mix to oklab(... / a). So every currentColor icon whose color is not black or white has this problem.

The harness can't catch it. mock-figma's createNodeFromSvg only checks for `^<svg` and reads width/height, and render.html rasterizes the SVG in Chrome, which understands oklch. That's why the diff stays clean.

Figma's SVG importer handles hex, rgb()/rgba(), hsl() and named colors, but not CSS Color 4 functions (oklch/oklab/lab/lch/color()). An unparseable paint is treated as unspecified. Unspecified fill falls back to black and unspecified stroke to none, so filled icons come in black and stroke icons (Heroicons outline, Lucide: fill="none" stroke="currentColor") come in invisible. I could not confirm this in live Figma; that part rests on known importer behavior.

The proposed fix is right in principle: parseColor() at line 480 already normalizes any CSS color to sRGB through a canvas. Its sketch has an ordering bug, though. SHAPE_PROPS lists 'fill' before 'fill-opacity' and 'stroke' before 'stroke-opacity', so an opacity attribute written while handling fill would be overwritten by the loop's next iteration with the raw computed fill-opacity, and the alpha would be lost. There is also no hex() helper in ui.html; one has to be added inside pageAgent. Setting val='none' when parseColor fails is also risky for unusual values such as context-fill, so keeping the original value is safer.

Regression risk is low. Values that are already rgb only change form (to hex), url(#grad) references and 'none' are left alone, and stop colors get the same treatment, which also fixes oklch gradient stops.

title: Inline SVG export drops CSS-only presentation: text font props, text-anchor, stroke-dashoffset, CSS transforms
evidence: robust-dashboard: (1) Chart axis labels styled by `.axis text{font-size:11px;font-family:Inter;font-weight:500}` lose all font properties, so the render draws large serif '100k', 'Jan'. (2) Month labels with `style="text-anchor: middle"` lose centering, because the style attribute is removed and text-anchor is not baked. (3) The '94' gauge label loses font-size:20, font-weight:700, text-anchor:middle and dominant-baseline:middle, so it is tiny and off-center. (4) Donut `.ring-value{stroke-dashoffset:75}` is lost: the JSON has stroke-dasharray="251.2" but no stroke-dashoffset, so a full ring is drawn instead of a 70% arc. (5) `class="-rotate-90"` on the <svg> (the standard progress-ring trick) is lost, so the arc starts at 3 o'clock. Donut/progress rings and CSS-styled chart text are ubiquitous in generated dashboards.
rootCause: ui.html svgNode(). It copies only SHAPE_PROPS (fill*, stroke, stroke-width/opacity/linecap/linejoin/dasharray, clip-rule, opacity) and STOP_PROPS. Then it removes every class and style attribute. Anything else that comes only from CSS is discarded: font-family, font-size, font-weight, font-style, letter-spacing, text-anchor, dominant-baseline, stroke-dashoffset, stroke-miterlimit, paint-order, visibility, transform. walk() also never looks at cs.transform for the svg element itself.
fix:
All changes are in ui.html svgNode().

1) Paint props. Extend SHAPE_PROPS with 'stroke-dashoffset', 'stroke-miterlimit', 'paint-order', 'visibility', 'marker-start', 'marker-mid' and 'marker-end'. The existing url() rewrite and px stripping already handle these values.

2) Text props. For tagName text, tspan or textPath, also bake TEXT_PROPS = ['font-family','font-size','font-weight','font-style','letter-spacing','word-spacing','text-anchor','dominant-baseline','alignment-baseline','baseline-shift','text-decoration-line'].
- Write font-size and letter-spacing without 'px'.
- Write letter-spacing only when it is not 'normal'.
- Write the text-decoration value as the 'text-decoration' attribute.
- Do this for every text element, not only CSS-styled ones, because the font is often inherited from HTML ancestors.

3) Normalize anchor and baseline so the result does not depend on how Figma's importer reads them. This applies to a <text> that has no positioned tspans and where text-anchor != 'start' or dominant-baseline is not auto/alphabetic:
```
const p = s.getStartPositionOfChar(0);   // baseline start after anchoring, in user units
const bb = s.getBBox();
d.setAttribute('x', p.x);
d.setAttribute('y', p.y);
d.setAttribute('text-anchor', 'start');
d.removeAttribute('dominant-baseline');
```
As a fallback for the baseline when the browser does not apply it to p.y, use y = bb.y + ascent, with ascent ≈ 0.8·fontSize.

4) Transforms on child elements. These may come from Tailwind v4's rotate/translate/scale properties, from transform, or from transform-origin/transform-box. Detect them with
```
const hasCss = ['transform','rotate','translate','scale'].some(p => scs.getPropertyValue(p) && scs.getPropertyValue(p) !== 'none');
```
If hasCss is true, i > 0, s is an SVGGraphicsElement, s.tagName is not 'svg', s is not inside defs/symbol/clipPath/mask/pattern, and both s.getCTM() and s.parentNode.getCTM() are non-null, then:
```
const m = s.parentNode.getCTM().inverse().multiply(s.getCTM());
d.setAttribute('transform', `matrix(${m.a} ${m.b} ${m.c} ${m.d} ${m.e} ${m.f})`);
```
This replaces any transform attribute, because a CSS transform overrides it. The browser has already resolved origin and box, so nothing needs to be re-implemented.

5) The root <svg>. Compose the matrix M from cs.translate, cs.rotate, cs.scale and cs.transform, in that order. Use DOMMatrix: translateSelf for translate, rotateSelf for rotate (parse 'Ndeg' and the axis forms; only rotation around z is supported), scaleSelf for scale, and multiplySelf(new DOMMatrix(cs.transform)). Apply it about the transform-origin (default 50% 50% of the untransformed CSS box, w0 = parseFloat(cs.width), h0 = parseFloat(cs.height)). Drop the translation part, because box is already the AABB from getBoundingClientRect.

If M is not the identity:
- Compute the viewBox-to-px mapping VB for the untransformed w0×h0 box, honouring preserveAspectRatio (default xMidYMid meet: s = min(w0/vbw, h0/vbh), tx = (w0 - vbw·s)/2 - vbx·s, and the same for ty).
- Map the four corners of 0..w0 × 0..h0 through T(origin)·M·T(-origin), and let T_aabb shift the min corner to 0,0.
- Wrap all of the clone's children in <g transform="matrix(T_aabb·T(o)·M·T(-o)·VB)">.
- Set the clone to viewBox="0 0 box.w box.h", width=box.w, height=box.h.

This handles any angle, including non-square boxes where -rotate-90 swaps w and h. A pure k·90° rotation of a square box reduces to rotate(θ cx cy) in viewBox units, as the original proposal said.

6) Separate follow-up, not part of this fix. Collect every url(#id) and href="#id" reference in the clone. Where the target is outside el, deep-clone it from the document into a <defs> in the clone, baked the same way. This fixes shared <symbol> sprites and shared gradients.

Regression safety: steps 1-2 only add explicit computed values, which match what the browser rendered. Steps 3-5 change geometry only when a non-default anchor, baseline or transform is present. The code stays ES2017-compatible (ui.html is not bound by the code.js restriction anyway).
verifierNotes:
Confirmed by reading the code and re-running the harness (robust-dashboard: diffPct 1.96, 0 mock errors).

Code: ui.html svgNode() (lines 939-967) bakes only SHAPE_PROPS (line 163) or STOP_PROPS into attributes. It then removes every class and style attribute. Nothing in ui.html reads transform, rotate, translate or scale for any element (grep finds no cs.transform), so CSS transforms are dropped everywhere.

dev/out/robust-dashboard.json confirms each claim:
- Axis <text> elements carry fill and stroke but no font-family, font-size or font-weight. Month labels have no text-anchor.
- The gauge text '94' is a bare <text x=50 y=50> with no font-size, font-weight, text-anchor or dominant-baseline.
- The ring-value circle has stroke-dasharray="251.2" but no stroke-dashoffset.
- The -rotate-90 svg has no rotation.

The render PNG shows all of it: large serif axis labels, a full green ring instead of a 70% arc, and a tiny '94' sitting off-centre. The orig PNG shows the intended result.

Recharts, Chart.js-in-SVG and hand-written charts rely on that. Once the SVG is serialized standalone, every inline-SVG text loses its font. So severity high is justified.

Tailwind v4 (the plugin's own TAILWIND_CDN, and the one this case uses) compiles rotate-*, -rotate-90, translate-* and scale-* to the individual CSS properties rotate:, translate: and scale:. With those, getComputedStyle().transform is 'none', so the cited -rotate-90 donut would still not be fixed. Child-element transforms should come from the browser's own geometry (getCTM), not from re-parsing transform-origin and transform-box by hand. The proposal's 'only if no transform attribute' rule is also wrong: a CSS transform overrides the SVG transform attribute.

- Whether Figma's SVG importer honours dominant-baseline (and maybe text-anchor) is not certain. Normalizing text positions is safer than relying on the attributes alone.

title: SVG <use> sprites and cross-SVG url(#id) references are emitted dangling, so icons and gradient fills vanish in Figma
evidence: robust-dashboard: the search and bell icons are `<svg><use href="#i-search"/></svg>` pointing at a hidden sprite <svg width=0 height=0>. The JSON SVG nodes contain only `<use href="#i-search" .../>`, and the render shows no search or bell icon. The area chart polygon has fill="url(#area)", but the gradient is defined in the sprite, so the area fill is missing. Figma's createNodeFromSvg resolves references only inside the given string.
rootCause: ui.html svgNode() clones only the element's own subtree. Referenced <symbol>, <linearGradient>, <radialGradient>, <clipPath>, <mask>, <pattern>, <filter> and <marker> definitions that live elsewhere in the document are not copied. The 0×0 sprite itself is dropped by walk() (box.w==0).
fix:
In ui.html `svgNode(el, box)`, after the existing bake loop and after the viewBox/width/height are set, add a reference-resolution pass. ES2017 is not required there, because this code runs in the agent page.

1. **Inline every `<use>` in the clone, deepest first.** Use a loop until no `<use>` remains, with a depth limit of 5.
   - Get `id` from `getAttribute('href') || getAttributeNS('http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink','href')`, with the leading `#` stripped.
   - Find the target with `S.doc.getElementById(id)`, using the iframe's document. If it is missing, remove the `<use>`.
   - Let `u` be the matching SOURCE `<use>`. Keep a Map from clone nodes to source nodes, built from the parallel `src`/`dst` arrays.
   - Build `g = <g>`. Copy the BAKED paint attributes from the clone `<use>` (fill, stroke, stroke-width, opacity and so on) onto `g`, so they are inherited exactly as in the shadow tree. Also copy `transform` if the `<use>` has one.
   - Let `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` be `u`'s x/y/width/height attributes. Width and height default to the clone's viewBox width/height when missing or set to "100%".
   - **If the target is a `<symbol>` (or `<svg>`):**
     - Let `vb` be the symbol's viewBox, defaulting to `0 0 w h`.
     - Use preserveAspectRatio xMidYMid meet unless the symbol says otherwise: `s = min(w/vbw, h/vbh)`, `tx = x + (w - vbw*s)/2 - vbx*s`, `ty` likewise.
     - Set `g.transform += translate(tx,ty) scale(s)`. If the attribute is "none", use separate sx/sy.
     - Append deep clones of the symbol's CHILDREN.
   - **Otherwise:** `g.transform += translate(x,y)` and append a deep clone of the target, with its `id` removed.
   - **Bake the inlined clones without breaking inheritance.** For each source descendant `s` and its parent `p` (both in the sprite), loop over SHAPE_PROPS/STOP_PROPS:
     - Let `v = cs(s)[prop]`.
     - If the raw attribute or inline style of `s` matches `/currentcolor/i` for that prop, set `color(u)`, the computed color of the `<use>`.
     - Else, if `prop` is inheritable and `v === cs(p)[prop]`, skip it, so the value is inherited from `g` as in the shadow tree.
     - Else set `v`.
     - Strip class and style.
   - Replace the clone `<use>` with `g`.

2. **Copy referenced paint servers and other defs.**
   - Collect ids from `url(#id)` in every attribute of every clone element (fill, stroke, clip-path, mask, filter, marker-start/mid/end) and from href/xlink:href on gradients and patterns.
   - For each id that is not already present in the clone (`clone.querySelector('[id="'+CSS.escape(id)+'"]')`), take `S.doc.getElementById(id)` and deep-clone it. Bake STOP_PROPS on stops and SHAPE_PROPS on clipPath, mask or pattern content, using the same bake helper.
   - Append it to a `<defs>` that is the first child of the clone, created if missing.
   - Repeat on the newly added defs until no new ids appear (gradient href chains, patterns that contain url refs). Cap at around 50 elements.

3. **Leave the rest alone.** Keep `walk()` dropping the 0×0 sprite, since it is still needed as the source. Do not rename ids: each `createNodeFromSvg` string is parsed on its own, so ids cannot collide across SVGs.

4. **Regression guard.** SVGs that have no `<use>` and no external url(#) refs go through this pass with no changes. Wrap the whole pass in try/catch and fall back to the current output if it fails.

5. **Test.** Re-run `node dev/fidelity.mjs robust-dashboard`. Expected: the search icon (slate-400 stroke) and bell icon appear, and the area chart polygon gets its indigo vertical gradient.
verifierNotes:
I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs robust-dashboard`: diff is 1.96%, with 0 mock errors. I compared the orig and render PNGs and the JSON.

1. **Search and bell icons.** The original shows both icons. The render shows neither. In the tree, the two SVG nodes are `<svg ...><use href="#i-search" .../></svg>` and `<svg ...><use href="#i-bell" .../></svg>`. Neither string contains a `<symbol>` or `<defs>`.

2. **Area chart.** The chart SVG's polygon has `fill="url(#area)"`, and the string has no `<linearGradient>` (I checked with a regex: false). The original shows a translucent indigo area under the bars. The render has none.

**Root cause.** It is as reported. `ui.html` `svgNode()` does `el.cloneNode(true)` and bakes computed paint only for the element's own subtree. It never resolves references to elements outside that subtree, and the 0×0 sprite is dropped by `walk()`. `code.js` `createNode()` then calls `figma.createNodeFromSvg(n.svg)` on that one isolated string. Figma's SVG parser only sees that string. So a dangling `<use>` produces nothing, or it throws and the catch puts in a placeholder rectangle. A dangling `url(#area)` falls back to no paint or black. In both cases the icon or the fill is lost in real Figma, not just in the harness renderer. `render.html` injects the string into a document that has no sprite, which matches Figma's behaviour here, so this is not a harness artifact.

**Impact.** Medium. Sprite icons (`<use href="#...">`) and gradients shared across SVGs show up in AI output and in pasted real-site HTML. Lucide or inline SVGs are more common, but when this happens the icons visibly disappear.

**Problems with the proposed fix:**
- **Baking order.** Calling getComputedStyle on `<symbol>` children while they sit in the hidden sprite resolves `currentColor` and inherited fill/stroke against the sprite's context, not the `<use>`. The values come back as plain rgb, so you can no longer find and rewrite "currentColor" afterwards. In this case that gives black or default paint instead of slate-400. - **Nested `<svg>` for symbols.** Figma's importer support for nested `<svg>` with viewBox, percentage width/height and preserveAspectRatio is uncertain. A computed `<g transform>` is safer.

   - Case "rendered": s is not inside defs, symbol, clipPath, mask, pattern or marker (test with s.closest(...)), and both s.getCTM() and s.parentNode.getCTM() are non-null. Then M = s.parentNode.getCTM().inverse().multiply(s.getCTM()).
   - Case "fallback": M = T(o)·new DOMMatrix(scs.transform)·T(-o). o is parsed from scs.transformOrigin (px). If scs.transformBox is 'fill-box', add s.getBBox().x and .y to o.
   - Then: d.setAttribute('transform', `matrix(${M.a} ${M.b} ${M.c} ${M.d} ${M.e} ${M.f})`). This also replaces the attribute that cloneNode copied, which is correct because the CTM already includes it.

   - Also: if scs.visibility === 'hidden', set display="none" (leaf shapes only). Add 'stroke-miterlimit' to SHAPE_PROPS (harmless).

2) Dash offset, baked into the pattern instead of relying on stroke-dashoffset:
   - Read P = parsed scs.strokeDasharray (numbers) and o = parseFloat(scs.strokeDashoffset). If s has a pathLength attribute, multiply both by s.getTotalLength()/pathLength and remove pathLength on d.
   - If P has odd length, use P = P.concat(P). L = sum(P). o' = ((o % L) + L) % L.
   - Walk P to find the index k where o' falls, and r = P[k] - (o' - start of segment k).
   - Q = [r, P[k+1..n-1], P[0..k-1], P[k] - r]. If k is even (a dash), append 0. If k is odd (a gap), prepend 0. Q now has even length and starts with a dash.

- fill (stretch): the original is distorted to fit the box. The render is a centred crop.
- scale-down: the original is a 160x80 image at natural size, centred on yellow. The render upscales it to 240x120.
- cover·left: barely visible here, because this image's aspect ratio is close to the box's.

dev/render.html draws FILL as background-size:cover and FIT as contain, both centred. That is exactly what Figma FILL/FIT do (Figma has no position for these modes), so this is a plugin bug, not a renderer artifact.

Severity: I'd call it medium, not high. The most common AI pattern, object-cover with centred position, already works. The broken cases are object-top/bottom portraits and hero crops, images stretched by the default object-fit:fill when the author omits object-cover, and none/scale-down (rare). They are noticeable but not page-breaking.

Assessment of the proposed fix: the core idea is correct. CROP + imageTransform [[cw/dw,0,-ox/dw],[0,ch/dh,-oy/dh]] maps the node's unit square into image-normalised space, with ox,oy being the image offset in the box (negative when it overflows). The identity transform under CROP stretches the image to the node, so fill works. Using a child rect when the image is smaller than the box is the right call, because a CROP transform reaching outside [0,1] is undefined or clamped in Figma.

But the proposed fix is incomplete or wrong in several places:
1. It only changes ui.html. code.js toPaint() drops imageTransform, so it must forward it.
2. dev/mock-figma.js keysOnly(['type','imageHash','scaleMode']) would reject imageTransform, and dev/render.html cannot draw CROP. The harness needs a matching update (outside my edit rights), or the fix will show up as mockErrors or a false diff.
3. object-fit applies to the content box. The transform has to be expressed relative to the node (border box), and padding/border must not show image, as on the .ringed avatar.
4. It needs guards for nw/nh == 0 (SVG without intrinsic size, or an image not yet loaded) and for computed values like calc() / 4-value object-position.
5. The video poster has no natural size on the element.

The corrected fix below addresses these.

title: Padding and border on are not honoured: the image is drawn under the border and padding
evidence: media-images `.ringed` (border 4px indigo + padding 4px white) and media-tw-icons `h-14 w-14 rounded-full bg-white p-1 ring-2` testimonial avatar: orig shows a white gap ring between the border and the photo. In render.png the photo fills the whole circle up to the border, so the gap is lost and the face is larger.
rootCause: ui.html imageNode(): pushes the IMAGE fill onto the same RECT as the bg/stroke, so it covers the border-box. CSS paints replaced content in the content box.
verifierNotes:
I checked the code. In ui.html, imageNode() builds one RECT whose fills are the background fills (v.fills) plus the IMAGE paint, sized to the border-box (`box`). canvasNode() and videoNode() do the same. code.js applyBox() then draws the border as strokeAlign='INSIDE' on top of that RECT. Padding is never read for replaced elements, which means:
(a) When there is padding, the background colour of the padding ring is completely covered by the photo.
(b) When there is a border, the photo is scaled to cover the border-box and the border hides its outer edge. CSS instead scales the photo into the content box, so the crop/zoom comes out different.

I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs media-images`. In that run the `.ringed` image did not load (it came out as a 127x34 alt-text box, one of 8 imagesMissing), so that case gave no evidence this time. The existing dev/out/media-tw-icons output does show the bug. The tree node `img · Leslie` is RECT 56x56 with fills [SOLID white, IMAGE FILL], radii 28, and a ring as a DROP_SHADOW spread 2. The Tailwind `p-1` padding left no trace in the tree. I cropped orig.png and render.png around the avatar. The original shows a white gap ring between the indigo ring and the photo. The render shows the photo filling the whole circle up to the ring, and the face is larger. So the gap is real and comes from the plugin, not from a renderer artifact.

The `h-14 w-14 rounded-full p-1 ring-2 bg-white` avatar and `border-4 border-white` avatars are very common in AI-generated testimonial and team sections. That makes this noticeable but not page-breaking, so medium.

The proposed fix (a FRAME at the border-box with a child RECT at the content box) is sound for the real Figma API. formNode() already returns a FRAME leaf with children positioned relative to the border-box. tryAutoLayout only runs for generic frames, not leaves. A FRAME with clipsContent clips to its corner radii, and frame strokes draw above children. I corrected and tightened four details:
1. Build it only when the insets are non-zero, so plain images stay a single RECT and the layer count does not grow.
2. Take the inner radii per corner from the adjacent horizontal and vertical insets, because Figma has no elliptical radii.
3. Get the coordinates from contentBox() minus the element rect, as formNode does. Do not compute them from `box`, which is relative to the parent.
4. Set constraints to STRETCH on the child, so the image follows the frame if the frame is later resized or stretched by Auto Layout. If code.js does not apply constraints yet, this needs a small addition there, or it can be skipped.

title: SVG images (, data:image/svg+xml, SVG backgrounds) are rasterized at their tiny intrinsic size
evidence: media-logos-masks: an SVG logo with width='24' height='8', displayed at 120x40, is rasterized to a 24x8 PNG (dev/out/media-logos-masks.json img0) and is visibly blurry in render.png. The SVG dot pattern in media-embeds becomes a 24x24 PNG. Logo clouds and illustrations are very often SVG files.
rootCause: ui.html imageBytes(): for blobs createImageBitmap rejects (SVG), `w = img.naturalWidth || rect*2`, so naturalWidth wins even when it is far below the display size. Vector data is thrown away.
verifierNotes: I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs media-logos-masks`. The first run timed out; the second completed with diffPct 3.27 and 0 mock errors. **What the tree shows.** In dev/out/media-logos-masks.json, img0 is the "acme svg" logo: an SVG with width='24' height='8' and viewBox 0 0 120 40, shown at 120x40. Its PNG header says 24x8. I cropped the logo row from orig.png and render.png. In the render the Acme logo is very blurry and the text cannot be read; the original is sharp. img1 is a viewBox-only SVG with no width/height. Chrome gives it a default size of 300x100, which is enough for a 120x40 display. So the bug only hits SVGs that declare width/height. **Root cause.** In ui.html, the SVG fallback in `imageBytes()` (around line 1102) does `w = img.naturalWidth || r.width*2`. Any declared intrinsic size wins, so the SVG is drawn at 1x its intrinsic size, or smaller. Background SVGs are worse: the call in boxVisual is `imageRef(url[1], null)`, so `el` is null and the code has no display size to fall back on. `imageRef()` also deduplicates by URL, so one PNG is shared by every place the image is used, whatever size each place shows it at. **Real-world impact.** The test case is contrived: an intrinsic size 5x smaller than the display size is rare. The common case is `` or 24px icon SVGs shown at their intrinsic size. Those come out as 1x rasters, which look soft on retina displays in Figma at 100% zoom and blurry when zoomed in or exported at 2x. Logo clouds and icons are often SVG files, so medium is right. **About the proposed fix.** - The raster part (scale up to at least 2x the displayed size) is correct, but it misses that background images get no display size at all. Their `el` is null, so `r` is null. - The "emit an SVG node via createNodeFromSvg" route is riskier than presented. Today these layers are RECTs with IMAGE fills, and they keep several things that an SVG node would drop: - object-fit as the fill's scaleMode - corner radii and clipping - the box's own fills and strokes - It would also lose any future image-filter handling: grayscale is already dropped today, which is a separate issue. - createNodeFromSvg throws on some real-world SVGs (external refs and other unsupported features). code.js would then show a placeholder, so this would need its own raster fallback. - Large illustrations would turn into thousands of vector layers. - Remote SVGs need a text fetch, which only works when CORS allows it. So the safe default is the higher-resolution raster. A vector path should only be an opt-in on top of it.

title: Raster fallbacks for vector sources: SVG /data-URI logos are rasterized at intrinsic 1x size
evidence: robust-mobile-shell@390: the `` logo (120×28) becomes img0, a 1,593-byte 120×28 PNG. It is blurry at any zoom or export above 1x and not editable. AI pages often use SVG data URIs for logos and placeholders.
rootCause: ui.html imageNode() always creates an IMAGE fill. In imageBytes(), the SVG branch draws via at naturalWidth × naturalHeight, which for SVGs with width/height attributes is the 1x CSS size.
verifierNotes: I checked this against the code and against harness output. The harness re-run failed with an ENOENT unlink race on dev/out/_orig_robust-mobile-shell.html, most likely another agent writing to dev/out at the same time. So I used the existing dev/out/robust-mobile-shell@390.json. In that file, images[0] (img0, url:null, which is the data URI) is a PNG whose IHDR header gives 0x78 by 0x1c, i.e. 120×28. That is exactly the 1x CSS size of the logo. The code path explains it. In ui.html, walk() case 'IMG' calls imageNode(), which always pushes an IMAGE fill via imageRef(). Later, loadImages() calls imageBytes(). fetch() of the data: URI succeeds and returns a blob of type image/svg+xml. sniff() returns null, and createImageBitmap rejects SVG blobs in Chrome, so the "SVG files can't go through createImageBitmap" branch runs: loadImg, then toPng(img, img.naturalWidth, img.naturalHeight). For an SVG with width/height attributes, naturalWidth/Height is the 1x size. The result is a 1x raster that cannot be edited. It looks soft on Retina screens even at 100% zoom and blurry at any zoom or export above 1x. A pixel diff taken at 1x cannot show this, which is why the harness doesn't flag it. The evidence is the bytes in the JSON. Severity is low to medium. Logos and placeholders as SVG data URIs or remote .svg files are common in AI-generated pages, but the layer is still in the right place and roughly right. The proposed fix has the right direction but four flaws: (1) walk() is synchronous. "Fetch the text / check the response content-type" cannot happen inside walk. Only data: URIs can be decoded synchronously there. Remote .svg files have to be handled after loadImages. (2) An SVG node in code.js goes through shapeNode's SVG branch, which never calls applyBox. A bare SVG node would therefore drop the img's own background, border, border-radius, box-shadow and padding. The current RECT path keeps them through boxVisual. (3) The createNode catch falls back to PLACEHOLDER. If createNodeFromSvg rejects the markup, a gray rectangle replaces a raster that would have worked: a regression. (4) object-fit cover/none need clipping, so a bare SVG can't express them. The proposal doesn't handle these. Its raster-scaling part, "max(natural, displayed*2)", is correct and safe. It should also apply to SVGs, not only to CSS backgrounds, as the minimum fix.

title: <iframe>/<object>/<embed> become a bare grey rectangle without the element's radius, border or shadow, and YouTube embeds lose their thumbnail
evidence: media-embeds: a YouTube iframe with rounded-2xl + box-shadow and a map iframe with a 2px border + radius 12 are both rendered as square #DBDBE0 rectangles without stroke or shadow.
rootCause: ui.html walk(): `case 'IFRAME': ... return leaf({type:'RECT', ..., fills:[PLACEHOLDER_FILL]})` skips boxVisual().
verifierNotes: This is confirmed in the code and in the tree output. In ui.html walk(), `case 'IFRAME': case 'OBJECT': case 'EMBED': case 'AUDIO': return leaf({ type: 'RECT', name: tag.toLowerCase(), ...box, fills: [PLACEHOLDER_FILL] })` returns before boxVisual() runs. IMG, CANVAS and VIDEO all go through boxVisual() plus boxed(). My re-run of `node dev/fidelity.mjs media-embeds` timed out waiting for window.__result, most likely because of network load or other agents running in parallel. So I checked the dev/out/media-embeds.json from the earlier run instead. Both iframes come out as `{"type":"RECT","name":"iframe",...,"fills":[{SOLID 0.86/0.86/0.88}]}` with no radii, stroke or effects. The CSS for them sets border-radius:16px plus box-shadow on `.embed`, and a 2px #e2e8f0 border plus radius 12 on `.map`. This is a plugin bug, not a renderer artifact. code.js would apply stroke, radii and effects if the tree carried them (applyStroke sets strokeAlign INSIDE and per-side weights). Severity stays low to medium: rounded YouTube and Google Maps embeds do show up on AI-generated landing and contact pages, but they are not on most pages. I also checked the thumbnail URL with curl: i.ytimg.com/vi/<id>/hqdefault.jpg returns `access-control-allow-origin: *`, so imageRef(url, null) can fetch it. The proposed fix has two flaws. (1) It says to add a play-button child to a RECT, but RECT nodes cannot have children in Figma or in code.js. When an overlay is added the node has to be a clipped FRAME. (2) Recursing into contentDocument for about:blank or srcdoc frames is risky (cross-origin errors, double offsets) and adds almost nothing, so it should be left out or limited to srcdoc with try/catch. The UA default iframe border (2px inset) will now become a stroke when the page does not reset it. That matches what the browser draws, so it is correct and not a regression.

title: <video> without a poster paints #1a1a1a over its own CSS background; no frame is captured
evidence: media-embeds: a `.video-noposter` with background #111827 renders as #1a1a1a (the JSON shows the SOLID bg followed by a second SOLID 0.1/0.1/0.1).
rootCause: ui.html videoNode(): always appends solid(0.1,0.1,0.1) when there is no poster.
verifierNotes: I confirmed this independently. In ui.html, videoNode() returns v.fills.concat(fill). When the video has no poster (or images are turned off), `fill` is always solid(0.1,0.1,0.1), and because it comes last it sits on top of the CSS background. I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs media-embeds` and checked dev/out/media-embeds.json. The 240px `.video-noposter` node has fills [SOLID r=0.07 (#111827), SOLID r=0.10]: the CSS background is there but completely hidden by the opaque #1a1a1a. In Chrome, a <video> with no poster and no decoded frame paints nothing over its box, so its CSS background shows through. If a frame has been decoded, Chrome shows that frame. The plugin gets both cases wrong. The poster-less video has no frame capture at all, while canvasNode() already captures pixels with toDataURL. This is a plugin bug, not a renderer artifact: the extra opaque SOLID really is in the tree that code.js builds. Real-world impact is low. Poster-less videos in AI-generated pages are uncommon, and #111827 vs #1a1a1a is a small colour shift, so I kept severity at low. The proposed fix is basically right. Three refinements: (1) gate the frame capture on videoWidth > 0 as well as readyState >= 2 (HAVE_CURRENT_DATA), so drawImage has real dimensions. (2) toDataURL throws SecurityError on a tainted canvas (cross-origin video without CORS), so wrap it in try/catch the way canvasNode does. (3) Use cs.objectFit for scaleMode. Chromium's UA stylesheet sets video { object-fit: contain }, so the computed style resolves to FIT by default, which matches browser letterboxing. Keeping the dark placeholder only when there is no CSS background preserves the existing intent (a visible "video" box) and adds nothing on top of authored backgrounds. No regressions for the poster case. All of this runs in the page agent, so code.js and the Figma API are untouched (IMAGE fills from data URLs already go through imageRef, as canvasNode shows).

title: Canvas snapshots can catch JS-animated charts mid-animation, WebGL canvases come out blank, and resolution is the backing store's
evidence: media-embeds: Chart.js animates for 1000 ms in JS (KILL_MOTION only affects CSS). The harness orig screenshot caught thin bars mid-animation while the agent caught them finished, so the result depends on timing. A chart created by IntersectionObserver on scroll (common) would be captured mid-animation by the plugin. Reasoning for WebGL: toDataURL on a webgl context without preserveDrawingBuffer returns a transparent image.
rootCause: ui.html canvasNode() snapshots whatever is in the backing store at extract time. Nothing finishes JS animations.
fix: In the agent, before the final settle(): if (window.Chart && Chart.instances) Object.values(Chart.instances).forEach(c=>{c.options.animation=false; c.stop&&c.stop(); c.update('none');}). Same idea for echarts (echarts.getInstanceByDom → setOption({animation:false})). For WebGL: call toDataURL inside a requestAnimationFrame callback, or check getContext('webgl2'||'webgl') and, if the pixels are all transparent, fall back to the placeholder plus the name 'canvas (WebGL)'.

title: Broken images become a nameless placeholder: alt text and the broken state are not carried
evidence: media-logos-masks: a 404 image (imagesMissing 1) gets an IMAGE fill with ref img6, bytes null and the url set. code.js then tries createImageAsync on the 404 URL and falls back to PLACEHOLDER. The browser showed the alt text 'Broken product photo'.
rootCause: ui.html imageNode() always emits an IMAGE paint when src is set, even when el.complete && el.naturalWidth===0. That also wastes a createImageAsync round-trip in code.js prepareImages().
fix:
No visual fix needed: the placeholder named after the alt text is the right Figma result. Optional cleanup to skip the useless createImageAsync call on 404s:
- In ui.html imageRef()/imageNode(), set `it.broken = true` only when all of these hold: el.complete, el.naturalWidth === 0, el.naturalHeight === 0, and the image is not SVG. Check that by requiring `!/^data:image\/svg|\.svg(\?|#|$)/i.test(src)`.
- In loadImages(), clear `broken` if the bytes fetch succeeded.
- In the `images` list sent to code.js, send `url: null` when `it.broken && !it.bytes`. prepareImages() then skips createImageAsync, toPaint() returns PLACEHOLDER, and the layer name keeps the alt text.

Do not add TEXT children or turn the RECT into a FRAME. Do not decide "broken" from a failed fetch in the UI, because CORS failures there are normal and Figma's URL fetch still loads those images.
verifierNotes: I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs media-logos-masks` (diffPct 3.27, imagesMissing 1, mockErrors 0) and read the JSON and diff PNG. 1. **"Nameless" is wrong.** imageNode() in ui.html names the layer `img · ${el.alt}`. The JSON shows the broken image as "img · Broken product photo", so the alt text is already carried in the layer name. 2. **The broken state is already handled.** In code.js, prepareImages() tries figma.createImageAsync(url). When that fails, toPaint() finds no hash for the ref and returns PLACEHOLDER. Figma therefore gets a grey placeholder rect at the right size, still named after the alt text and keeping its dashed stroke from boxVisual(). For a design tool this is the right result. Chrome's broken-image icon plus inline alt text is browser error UI, and copying it into the design would be a regression, not better fidelity. The red pixels in the diff come only from Chrome's alt text and icon, which is that error UI. 3. **The proposed fix has problems:** - A RECT cannot have children, so "a small TEXT child" means turning the image into a FRAME, which changes the structure for no design benefit. - The check el.complete && !el.naturalWidth is not a safe "broken" test. An SVG `` that only has a viewBox (like "no size svg" in this same case) can report naturalWidth 0 depending on the engine, but it decoded fine and has bytes (img1 bytes=true). The fix would wrongly turn real logos into placeholders. - You cannot skip createImageAsync just because the UI's fetch failed. CORS-blocked images fail in the UI but load through Figma's URL fetch, which is exactly why prepareImages() falls back to it. What is left is a small inefficiency: one extra createImageAsync request to a 404 URL. It has no visible effect, so I judge the finding not a real fidelity gap.

title: preserveAspectRatio='none' SVGs (wave/section dividers) depend on unverified Figma importer behaviour
evidence: media-svg wave divider: viewBox 0 0 1440 320 drawn in 1440x80 with preserveAspectRatio=none. The harness renders it in Chrome, so it looks correct there. Whether Figma's createNodeFromSvg honours 'none' is unverified (reasoning only); if it doesn't, the wave comes out letterboxed or overflowing.
rootCause: ui.html svgNode() forwards preserveAspectRatio as is and relies on the importer.
fix: When the viewBox aspect differs from the box aspect: for preserveAspectRatio='none', wrap the clone's children in <g transform="scale(boxW/vbW, boxH/vbH) translate(-vbx,-vby)"> and set viewBox to '0 0 boxW boxH'. For the default meet/slice, compute the uniform scale plus alignment offset the same way. The SVG Figma receives then always has a viewBox that matches the box 1:1.
